name: benchmark_v1
purpose: Frozen, held-out evaluation set for the trained AntID model. Created because the original training-time val split (top1=0.666/top3=0.819, recorded in training/artifacts/eval.json) could not be reproduced: data/manifest_all.csv was regenerated after training, which rewrote the split column and row order that val_split.json now pins going forward. Re-evaluating the trained weights against any split reconstructable from the current manifest scores ~93% top-1 -- that number is memorization, not skill, and must never be reported as a result. This benchmark sidesteps the whole problem: instead of trying to recover the old split, it draws an entirely new, independently-verified-unseen sample.
exclusion_criteria: Structural (primary guarantee): only observations with created_at on or after 2026-06-16 were eligible -- one full day after the training scrape's later wave completed (wave 2, 2026-06-14 16:49 -04:00). An observation that did not exist at training scrape time cannot be a photo the model was trained on, independent of any ID bookkeeping.
Explicit photo_id exclusion: every candidate was checked against the photo_id column of data/manifest_all.csv (9989 rows) before being kept.
Verified zero overlap after the fact on three independent axes: photo_id, observation_uuid, and sha256 image hash (see verification block below).

verification.method: Training photo_id -> observation_uuid was reconstructed by re-querying the iNat API per species, anchored at created_d2=2026-06-14 (the training scrape's own cutoff) so the ordering matches what the original scraper actually saw. 9920/9989 training photos (99.3%) resolved to an observation_uuid this way; the remainder are very likely observations since deleted, made private, or downgraded from research-grade -- unreachable by definition, not a gap in the method. Training image sha256 was computed directly from the 9981 locally cached files under data/clean/.
verification.note: One internal duplicate was found and removed before this count: two different photo_id/observation_uuid pairs (leptomyrmex-erythrocephalus, uploaded 3 days apart) had byte-identical image content, i.e. the same photo re-submitted as a second observation. This is not a training leak -- it was a duplicate within the fresh scrape itself -- but was removed for benchmark cleanliness. Original scrape yielded 1592 images; final benchmark is 1591.

low_sample_species_warning.note: anoplolepis-custodiens and polyrhachis-schistacea have only 1 image each in this benchmark -- not enough recent (post-cutoff) research-grade iNat observations existed to reach the 35-image target, and the shortfall was not backfilled by loosening the date cutoff or the quality_grade=research requirement. Their individual per-species top-1/top-3 figures are NOT statistically meaningful (a single trial is either 0% or 100%) and must not be read as evidence of model performance on those species specifically. They are kept in the benchmark rather than dropped, and do contribute to the overall micro-average and to the per-species macro-average like any other class; readers should look at the overall/macro numbers and treat these two rows as informational only.

scope.note: This benchmark measures classification accuracy among the 50 species the model was trained on -- nothing else. It is drawn entirely from photos of those 50 species, so it cannot and does not measure what happens when the input is an ant outside that set. The system has no 'unknown' or 'none of these' outcome: an out-of-scope ant is always forced into whichever of the 50 trained classes scores highest, confidently. Improving the classifier architecture does not address this by itself -- closing that gap needs both broader species coverage and an explicit low-confidence/reject path, which would need its own separate out-of-scope evaluation set to measure (this one cannot be repurposed for that).
scope.measures: accuracy among the 50 trained species only
scope.does_not_measure: behavior on ants outside the 50 trained species

tuning_policy.note: Do not use this benchmark as a tuning or model-selection signal. It exists to report one number for a finished model, not to pick among candidates during development -- repeatedly evaluating variants against it and keeping the best score would slowly turn it into a validation set the model is indirectly fit to. Tune against a freshly pinned val_split.json from the candidate's own training run instead, and evaluate only the finalized model here.
